messages:
lina (runtime): quick follow-up from the RFC — thinking about compacting in-flight sets to reduce queue fragmentation and memory churn
kevin (scheduler): curious, can you sketch the compacting idea? sounds like coalescing but at inflight set level
maria-ml: +1 for sketch. also worried about latency regressions if we compact too eagerly
lina (runtime): idea: maintain per-lane in-flight buckets keyed by (tenant, model-variant, kv-affinity). periodically "compact" by merging small buckets into a single compact window if they are below a threshold (count or estimated token budget)
kevin (scheduler): so instead of many tiny microbatches we form a compact batch that still keeps kv-affinity best-effort? how do we avoid mixing tenants that hurt fairness
lina (runtime): fairness preserved by tagging merged buckets with a soft-quota token weight. we keep admission credits per-tenant and adjust compacted window weights proportionally
jordan-sre: sounds like a credit-smoothing policy. what about preemption? if a high-priority tenant arrives do we split the compacted bucket or preempt it
maria-ml: splitting mid-inflight is messy for kv-cache and stream semantics. preemption that flushes compacted buckets might be safer but could cost tokens
kevin (scheduler): tradeoff table we discussed in the RFC: split->keeps latency but increases overhead; flush->simpler but wastes work. maybe hybrid: compacted windows are eligible for soft-preempt where we stop accepting more requests but finish already started microbatches
lina (runtime): that was my thought too. implementation detail: compact windows carry a mutable head pointer. if preempt needed, we mark window.read_only=true and let it drain. new arrivals routed to fast-path lanes
sre-bot: deploy-check: load test harness needed to validate head-of-line blocking under bursty arrivals :warning:
kevin (scheduler): instrumentation we need: per-window queue length, merge-count, average merge latency, kv-cache hit rate per-window, and percent-of-windows-soft-preempted
maria-ml: and quality metrics: sample prompt sets to ensure compacting doesn't degrade generation distribution (esp. for long-context models)
jordan-sre: ops concern: memory accounting. compacting groups reduce pointer overhead but aggregated windows must have correct backpressure signals to upstream proxies
lina (runtime): agreed. we should add a per-window virtual token-accounting field so proxies can see effective headroom. proto config snippet I mocked: 
```
compact_policy:
  enabled: true
  min_count: 4       # smallest buckets to consider
  max_compact_tokens: 1024
  merge_interval_ms: 20
  soft_quota_weight: 0.7
```
kevin (scheduler): merge_interval_ms is critical — too small and we don't gain batching; too big and p99 latency suffers. I propose an adaptive interval: proportional to recent inter-arrival percentiles
maria-ml: adaptive interval needs to be stable under correlated arrivals (we saw oscillations earlier in sim runs)
lina (runtime): yes, add hysteresis and decay. also a minimum/maximum bound and a fast-exit if a high-priority request appears
jordan-sre: what about admission API changes? current enqueue contract expects per-request deadline_hint. we can add a window_hint to allow proactive compaction: 
```json
{"deadline_hint_ms":120, "window_hint":"joinable"}
```
kevin (scheduler): window_hint would be backward-compatible; default is "exclusive" meaning don't join; value "joinable" lets runtime consider compaction
lina (runtime): we should be conservative by default. expose knob in customer routing policies as well (some tenants opt out)
maria-ml: perf testing plan: synthetic bursts with mixed weight tenants, and real-capture replay (week of traffic) to validate token-per-cost delta and quality A/B
sre-bot: checklist: unit tests for merge correctness, integration test with kv-cache warm/cold scenarios, perf harness for 95/99/99.9 latency buckets
kevin (scheduler): long-term refactor: abstract Window class and decouple coalescer from admission. today they're intertwined which makes reasoning hard. split responsibilities: Coalescer (policy) -> WindowManager (lifecycle) -> Admission (credits)
lina (runtime): that refactor will allow us to plugin alternative coalescers (latency-first, cost-first, tenant-isolation)
maria-ml: sounds good. timeline?
lina (runtime): propose spike this week with prototype in feature branch, perf harness by EOW, and RFC follow-up with numbers early next week
jordan-sre: +1. I'll allocate staging clusters for the replay tests
kevin (scheduler): I'll draft the Window abstraction and API; will push a design doc to the RFC thread
maria-ml: will prepare eval prompts and baseline metrics to watch for regressions
lina (runtime): thanks all. small action items: kevin doc, maria eval set, jordan staging, lina prototype. tagging @kevin and @jordan for follow-ups :thumbsup:
kevin (scheduler): ack. starting doc now
jordan-sre: ack — will post cluster details once provisioned
lina (runtime): ending notes: watch out for headroom signaling races — add sequence numbers to window updates to avoid stale overwrite
maria-ml: and add an alert for kv-cache drop > 5% after rollout
kevin (scheduler): noted. closing thread, will link PRs here as they appear :rocket:
